problem: validate_bounds is now a no-op that reference_impl.parse calls via self, so unbounded ends marked closed such as (None,5,True,False) or the 2-tuple (None,5) are accepted instead of raising ValueError and yield invalid results closed at infinity.

Converting 4-tuple flags with bool() before delegating means the reference's isinstance(flag, bool) check can never fail, so values like 0/1, None or "no" are silently accepted as flags instead of raising ValueError.

The rebuilt tuple makes error messages report altered input instead of what the caller passed, and bool() on the flags lets exceptions other than ValueError escape parse, breaking its ValueError-only error contract.

Production code now imports the unpackaged reference_impl module and calls its private _Algebra.parse on a foreign instance, which pyright flags, breaks import when the file is absent, and makes any differential test against the reference compare parsing with itself.
The parse docstring that documented its return shape and ValueError contract was deleted.
The branch changes input validation in parse and validate_bounds (lines 10-16) without adding any tests, and the repository has none, so the F1 and F2 regressions go undetected.
